title: Nettle Finds Lumina's Nap
markdown:
Once, in the sparkly Cloudy Hills, lived a young elf named Nettle. Nettle had hair the colour of soft green moss and eyes that twinkled like dewdrops. He was a kind elf, always ready with a smile. His very best friend was Lumina, a beautiful moon-moth. Lumina’s wings were like little pieces of the moon, dusted with stars. When she flew, they made a soft whirr-whirr sound, like tiny fairy bells.

One evening, the air in the Cloudy Hills felt warm and soft, like a cozy blanket. Nettle knew it was time for Lumina’s nap. Lumina liked to nap in the warmest, coziest spot she could find.

“Where shall we go tonight, Lumina?” Nettle whispered.

Lumina twitched her little feelers. She did not fly to her usual branch.

Nettle’s heart did a little flip, a happy ready-to-help flip. “Don’t worry, Lumina,” he said, his voice warm and kind. “We’ll find your perfect nap spot. I promise!”

Lumina’s wings shimmered, a soft glow that seemed to say, Oh, I hope so.

So Nettle and Lumina set off into the Warm Lantern Woods. This wood was a magical place. The trees had leaves that glowed with a soft warm light, like pretty lanterns. They made the ground glow with a cozy dappled light. The air smelled like sweet honey and happy dreams.

“Maybe under the big blue flower?” Nettle suggested. He pointed to a big blue flower taller than him. It chimed when the wind blew. Lumina fluttered closer. She landed lightly on a soft petal and sipped a tiny drop of dew. Sip, sip. Then, with a little shake of her wings, she flew back to Nettle. Not quite right for her nap.

“Ah, but we must keep looking!” Nettle said. They walked past a cave where little crystals twinkled like stars. The light was bright, but Lumina flew right past.

“Too sparkly tonight, Lumina?” Nettle asked kindly.

Lumina made a soft whirr-whirr.

As they walked on a path with soft fluffy snow—yes, soft snow in the warm wood, because that is a special thing about the Cloudy Hills—they saw a little person ahead. It was Wizard Pipkin! Wizard Pipkin was a friendly wizard with twinkly eyes and a big backpack. His backpack was full of chalk. He had chalk for drawing sunny days, chalk for drawing happy giggles, and chalk for drawing cozy corners.

“Hello, Nettle! Hello, Lumina!” Wizard Pipkin chirped. “What are you doing out tonight?”

“Oh, Wizard Pipkin,” Nettle said. “We’re looking for Lumina’s perfect nap spot. We haven’t found it yet.”

Wizard Pipkin chuckled, like little bells tinkling. “The hunt for the coziest corner! A very important job!” He looked in his backpack. “Perhaps a little help from my chalk will show us!” He held up yellow chalk, bright and soft like sunshine. “This is chalk for finding sunny spots. Let’s draw a sun.”

Nettle drew a little sun on a stone. The sun glowed warmly for a moment, then faded. Lumina watched, but she did not settle.

“Hmm,” said Nettle. “Not the spot for napping.”

Wizard Pipkin pulled out another chalk. This one shimmered like moonlight. “And this is chalk for finding peaceful places. Let’s see!” He drew a moon shape on a leaf. The moon pulsed with a soft light. Lumina fluttered around it, then flew back to Nettle.

Wizard Pipkin’s eyes twinkled. “Sometimes the best spots are the surprises. They are the quiet finds.” He reached into his backpack one last time and pulled out chalk the colour of twilight. It smelled like sweet lavender. “This,” he whispered, “is chalk for finding quiet comfort. Let’s try it near those rustling bushes.”

He drew a soft swirl on the ground near bushes whose leaves whispered secrets. The chalk swirls hummed a very quiet sleepy tune.

They did not hurry the next look. Nettle sat on a lantern-lit root and let Lumina rest on his sleeve. One leaf finished dripping its gold. Pipkin waited, twilight chalk in his hand.

Then Nettle saw it. Just behind the whispering bushes, where the lantern light dripped through the leaves, was a little hollow. It was lined with the softest moss, and a single lantern leaf cast a warm golden glow right into it. It was, Nettle knew, the most peaceful, most comfortable, most perfect nap spot Lumina could ever want.

Lumina, with a happy little flutter, darted toward it. Whirr-whirr! Her wings shimmered with joy. She snuggled into the moss, her starlight wings tucking around her like a soft cloak. Nettle watched her, his heart feeling as warm and happy as the golden light. He sat down beside the hollow.

Lumina closed her tiny moth eyes, breathing softly. Nettle yawned a big elf yawn. The warm light was so soothing, and the gentle hum of the chalk was like a lullaby. Nettle’s own eyes started to feel heavy too. He snuggled down beside the hollow, Lumina’s gentle whirr-whirr a soft song beside him.

And there, in the Warm Lantern Woods, with the sweet honey smell and the soft lantern light, young Nettle and his dear moon-moth Lumina drifted into the sweetest coziest sleep. The Cloudy Hills kept watch. The usual branch, back home, stayed empty, and did not mind.
characters: Nettle (young elf of the Cloudy Hills), Lumina (star-dusted moon-moth)
